originalRequest: Produce the English variant of the shipped Chinese course learn-agent-observability for learn.agentmentor.dev. Teaching rewrite in English (not a translation): same 6-lesson structure, same lesson slugs, same interactive-block ids and answer positions, source quotes restored to their verbatim English originals from sources.md, runnable code kept logic-identical with only comments and user-facing strings translated, cross-course references pointing at the live English course titles, natural desk-voice English prose with no AI-slop register.

briefCompleteness.evidence: The owner ratified the multilingual plan explicitly: all six locales on learn.agentmentor.dev, English first, batches of 2-3 courses in path order with a commit per course. The zh course is the verified source of truth for scope, learner model, structure, and grounding, so no additional clarification was needed.

learnerModel.targetReader: A developer who has finished the first ten courses in this series, runs an eval track, and wants to trace an agent failure to the exact step instead of guessing
knownConcepts: Hand-writing a stop_reason-driven harness loop and tool_use/tool_result pairing (course 7)
The eval track and metrics beyond pass rate (course 10)
Basic JavaScript / Node.js reading and writing
unknownConcepts: Raw transcripts as first-hand evidence vs the agent's self-report
Structured logging and metrics design for a harness
Trace trees, correlation IDs, and subagent nesting
How the telemetry pipeline itself lies (silent failures, batch loss)
Hooks as probes at loop lifecycle gates
A debugging workflow built for non-deterministic runs
learnerModel.assumedEnvironment: A Node.js environment, terminal access, a text editor, and the course-7 harness code available to extend
learnerModel.firstIndependentAction: Take one failed run of their own agent and list which questions they cannot currently answer from the artifacts they have
noviceRamp: Lesson 1 names the problem — one symptom over several externally indistinguishable causes — before any tooling
Lesson 2 establishes the evidence hierarchy: raw transcript first, self-report never
Lesson 3 adds structured logs and metrics; lesson 4 threads them into a trace tree with correlation IDs
Lesson 5 places hook probes at the loop's gates and walks the non-determinism-aware localization workflow
Lesson 6 wires the full observability layer onto the course-7 harness and runs one symptom-to-fix drill

learnerBrief: The target reader has finished the first ten courses, runs an eval track, and reads JavaScript. Evals tell them pass/fail but not why. The course gets them to treat raw transcripts as first-hand evidence, design structured logs and metrics, thread records into trace trees with correlation IDs, place hook probes at the loop's gates, and finally wire a complete observability layer onto the course-7 harness and walk one full symptom-to-fix debugging drill.
scope: Covered: why non-determinism breaks reproduce-then-debug, raw transcripts as evidence, structured logging and metrics for a harness, trace trees with correlation IDs and subagent nesting, telemetry-pipeline failure modes, hooks as lifecycle probes, a localization workflow (filter by prompt id, find first divergence, replay stepwise), and a hands-on observability layer (JSONL logs + trace-tree printing + metrics rollup). Not covered: specific observability platforms (named only where citations name them), alert thresholds and SLO design (no first-party numbers exist), and course 10's eval methodology (the same metrics score there and diagnose here). Depth: from zero to tracing one real symptom to the step that caused it.

qualitySelfReview.diagramUse: Diagrams are kept exactly where the zh original uses them (the trace-tree structure), with labels rewritten in English; none added or removed. A span tree is the diagram-shaped content of this course, and the zh placement was already review-validated.
weakestPoints: The sources.md writing-discipline rules are strict here — the five-step debugging workflow is the course's own arrangement and repro techniques carry no citations by design; readers wanting authority for those sections must treat them as engineering practice, which the text says explicitly
Telemetry pipeline failure modes are taught against one CLI's documented behavior; other stacks fail differently
The OTEL_* env-stripping negative result is version-bound product behavior and dated in the text

As an English teaching rewrite of a verified zh course, idiomatic drift is the residual risk: source quotes were restored verbatim and code kept logic-identical, but prose was re-taught rather than translated, so review must check meaning-equivalence against the zh lessons
followUpChecks: Render pass on learn.agentmentor.dev /en/agent-observability/... after deploy: all 6 lessons plus README, interactive cards hydrate
Verify every glossary term appears verbatim in the en lessons (attach check)
Verify every [^Sn] anchor in en lessons has a matching ## Sn block in en sources.md
Confirm the six check-block ids and correct-answer positions are byte-identical to zh (c/a/b/c/a/b in lesson order)
Re-run the capstone JS (JSONL logging, trace-tree print, metrics rollup, HEAD_CHARS=0 privacy tier) and confirm outputs match the asserted logs

acceptanceReview.terminalTask: The learner can wire a harness with an observability layer — one structured record per model request and tool call, a trace tree threaded by correlation IDs, a metrics rollup — then take one 'can't say why' symptom, filter by prompt id, find the first divergence, replay with identical inputs, fix, and show the re-run comparison.
acceptanceReview.interactionCheck: Six agentmentor-check blocks, one per lesson (rerun-to-reproduce in L1, summary-vs-transcript in L2, error-count-lies in L3, silent-telemetry in L4, hook-otel-shortcut in L5, log-everything in L6), preserved from the zh variant with identical ids, modes, choice counts, and correct-answer positions; label, prompt, whyHere, choice text, and feedback are English teaching rewrites specific to each lesson's misconception. Exercises keep the zh Level structure with rubric, answer, and hints per Level.
acceptanceReview.learnerFitCheck: The course assumes the prior ten courses: the harness loop, the eval track, and JavaScript. Evidence hierarchy, logging design, tracing, hooks, and the localization workflow are taught from zero in dependency order; the learner first assembles the full layer in lesson 6, after every prerequisite. Lesson 1's first exercise asks only for an unanswerable-questions audit of the reader's own failed run.
promotionNotes: English variant of a shipped zh course: structure, grounding, and answer positions inherited from the verified original
All interactive blocks preserve id/mode/choice-count/correct-answer byte-parity with zh

The review-resolved L5/L6 seam declarations (step mapping, stub-vs-real reconciliation, tool-span nesting difference, field-vocabulary table) preserved in English

memoryBoundary: This agentmentor.json is a course-local state record, stored only in the course directory for quality checks and learning-path tracking. It is never written back to Claude Code or any host AI system's long-term memory and does not affect other courses or conversations.
